description:
Mirrors GitHub issue #35 (https://github.com/theodoreOnzGit/outram-park-backend/issues/35), posted 2026-08-31. Full architectural redesign of the kovan crate from 'PDF workbench with digitiser tabs' into a human-first, Git-native scientific literature wiki.

NORTH STAR (issue s49): 'If Kovan disappeared tomorrow, would the repository still be understandable and useful?' Tracked human-readable files (Markdown, BibTeX, TOML, PDFs, Git) are authoritative; .kovan/ is disposable derived state and 'rm -rf .kovan' must always be safe.

OWNERSHIP BOUNDARIES (s1, s47.5-6): kopitiam-pdf owns PDF interaction, kopitiam-neovim owns text editing, kopitiam-ocr owns OCR, kopitiam-bibliography owns BibTeX identity. Kovan owns research semantics and synchronisation ONLY. Do NOT implement replacement PDF, Vim, or OCR engines inside kovan.

TWO AMENDMENTS agreed in the issue thread:
  1. A paper's id IS its BibTeX citekey -- no separate citekey field. bibliography.bib is the single authoritative identity namespace; the paper directory, its markdown filename, its wiki-link target and its citation key are all literally the same string. Consequence: citekey uniqueness enforced at ingestion, and citekey rename becomes a transactional repo-wide refactor.
  2. crates/kovan-literature's ARCHIVE DATA (open/, proprietary/, generated/, docs/, derived/) moves out into its own repo (working name outram-park-lit) and comes back as a git submodule. The Rust crate stays in crates/kovan-literature. Tracked as a separate parallel track, not part of the numbered sequence.

SURVEY DONE (s47.2-3), 2026-08-31 @ 5e504e3f: crates/kovan/src is 19,811 lines / 44 files. The keep/adapt/migrate/replace/delete-after-parity map is committed at crates/kovan/docs/kovan-redesign-migration-map.md. Headline: ~3,100 lines delete-after-parity (the duplicated PDF reader + annots), ~1,850 replace/adapt, ~14,800 keep. This is NOT a rewrite -- s47.8 explicitly forbids rewriting code merely because the architecture differs.

TWO EXTERNAL BLOCKERS:
  - step 11 needs kopitiam-pdf 0.3.2+ (kopitiam#96). Latest published is 0.3.1, whose features are default=[kpdf], kpdf=[eframe,egui,rfd] -- the separate 'egui' feature the refactor describes exists in NO published version.
  - steps 5 and 12-16 need kopitiam-bibliography (op-k25f), unpublished; maintainer will publish as v0.0.1.

s45 NON-GOALS -- do not prematurely build: detailed graph/table digitiser redesign, AI assistant UI, LLM integration, vector search, cloud sync beyond Git, elaborate semantic ontology, AI summaries, fancy mindmap physics before the model works.
title: kovan: Git-native literature wiki redesign (GitHub issue #35)

description:
From the sod_shock_tube_timed_series measurement (2026-09-14, release, 100 cells, exact Riemann as arbiter):

  dt (s)   steps   wall(s)  ns/cell-step  L2 rho     L2 u      L2 p
  8.0e-6     791    0.038      485.0      1.3710e-2  1.4824e1  1.0016e3
  4.0e-6    1581    0.063      396.2      1.3947e-2  1.5133e1  1.0385e3
  2.0e-6    3162    0.131      415.8      1.4054e-2  1.5148e1  1.0503e3
  1.0e-6    6325    0.254      402.1      1.4108e-2  1.5157e1  1.0565e3
  5.0e-7   12649    0.504      398.6      1.4139e-2  1.5197e1  1.0612e3

Two findings.

1) Cost is linear at ~400 ns per cell-step, flat across a 16x sweep (the 485 at the coarsest run is warm-up over only 791 steps). No hidden superlinearity.

2) Refining dt does not improve the answer -- L2 density creeps UP from 1.371e-2 to 1.414e-2 across 16x refinement. The error is spatially dominated on the fixed 100-cell mesh and the temporal term is already negligible at dt = 8e-6 (acoustic CFL ~0.03).

So the committed validation case at dt = 1e-6 is ~8x more expensive than it needs to be and returns a marginally worse L2 than dt = 8e-6. NOT changed here: the committed timestep is part of a validated configuration and moving it is a maintainer decision, not a side effect of adding a timing test.

Follow-up worth doing: the series that actually probes the binding constraint is over MESH RESOLUTION, which would show the expected spatial order. That needs outram-foam-mesh's block_mesh to generate meshes at several resolutions, and outram-foam-appbuilder-lib does not currently depend on it (not even as a dev-dependency). Adding that edge for a timing test was judged out of scope in this session; it is the right next step.
title: outram-foam-appbuilder-lib: Sod validation runs at 8x the timestep cost it needs; and the series worth running is over mesh, not dt

description:
The sim paces against a native wall clock (app_scaffold/real_time_pacing.rs). In a browser it must pace against requestAnimationFrame AND survive being backgrounded — browsers throttle inactive tabs to roughly 1 Hz.

Needs an explicit, documented decision rather than a default: wall-clock-locked (sim time tracks real time, tab throttling means the sim visibly stalls), or fixed-step-with-catch-up (sim advances a bounded number of steps on return, with a cap so a tab left open overnight does not attempt hours of catch-up on one frame).

Whichever is chosen, say so in the docs — a user who backgrounds a reactor transient and returns to a different answer than they expected deserves to know which model they are in. GH #39 Phase 6.
title: Phase 6: real-time pacing against requestAnimationFrame, incl. backgrounded tabs

description:
Port GSL's specfunc/expint.c (gsl_sf_expint_E1) and specfunc/gamma_inc.c (gsl_sf_gamma_inc) into petir.

WHY: njoy ACER's MF=5 LF=12 (Madland-Nix) is blocked on fmn (acefc.f90:9155), which needs the exponential integral e1 and incomplete gamma gami. gh:#201 originally scoped that as transcribing ~400 lines of SLATEC Chebyshev tables, verified against SLATEC. That is now the WRONG plan: GSL has both, GSL is vendored and licence-verified here, and GSL can be compiled and run as a code-to-code oracle (proven for the cheb module: 6114 values, 77% bit-identical, and GSL's own coefficients through our evaluator 5025/5025 BIT-identical).

DO: port from GSL, verify against (a) GSL's own specfunc/test_gamma.c + test_sf.c, ported, and (b) GSL compiled+run, same method as reference-data/gsl/.

THEN: implement fmn in njoy-outram-park-fork on top, then the LF=12 branch (acefc.f90:7037-7126), which is routine.

CAVEAT for the maintainer: njoy-outram-park-fork is deliberately dependency-lean (its CLAUDE.md: thiserror, uom; no BLAS). Taking petir is a new dependency edge -- petir is no_std with only libm, about as light as possible, but that is a maintainer call.

See gh:#201 comment for the full revised analysis.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
PROGRESS 2026-09-14 (cce9bba0e): E1 IS DONE. petir::expint_e1 + expint_e1_scaled port specfunc/expint.c's expint_E1_impl and specfunc/cheb_eval.c. All 150 coefficients across the six Chebyshev series were EXTRACTED BY SCRIPT from the C source, not retyped -- that was the transcription risk gh:#201 flagged, now removed. Verified against GSL compiled+run: 480 values, 96.0 % bit-identical, worst rel 3.116e-16 (reference + driver committed to reference-data/gsl/).

REMAINING: gsl_sf_gamma_inc. Closure MEASURED, not guessed: gamma_inc.c 721 + gamma.c 1685 + psi.c 866 + zeta.c 1050 + erfc.c 465 = ~4800 lines, because gamma_inc calls gsl_sf_{erfc,exp_err,gamma,gammastar,lngamma,log_1plusx_mx}_e. That is its own pass, not a tail on this one. Oracle side already solved: the driver in reference-data/gsl/ links gamma_inc.c successfully, so a reference can be generated the same way.

NOTE for whoever picks it up: fmn only ever calls gami at a = 1.5, and gamma(3/2,x) has a closed form in erf that would shrink this enormously -- but using it would be DERIVING rather than porting, which op-chyp decision 2 forbids. If the maintainer wants that exception it should be recorded deliberately, not slipped in.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
DONE 2026-09-14 (6b230a234). Both functions ported and ACER's LF=12 wired.

E_1: 480 values vs GSL compiled+run, 96.0 % bit-identical, worst rel 3.1e-16.
gamma_inc: P(a,x) 1320 values 1278 bit-identical worst 7.1e-15; lower gamma worst 9.3e-15; gami(3/2,x) -- the path fmn takes -- 220 points worst 1.9e-15.
All 239 coefficients across both ports EXTRACTED BY SCRIPT, not retyped.

The ~4800-line closure estimate was the WHOLE of gamma_inc; the a=3/2 path is far smaller (Q_asymp_unif is a>1e6 only, dropping erfc entirely; lngamma takes only Lanczos; gammastar only gstar_a). Unreachable branches REFUSED with their upstream line, not shipped untested.

Two things worth carrying forward: (1) my first continued fraction was GUESSED and had three conflicting bindings -- caught and replaced with the transcription; (2) the first oracle driver computed lower gamma as Gamma(a)-Gamma(a,x), which is catastrophic cancellation (wrong by 1.391e-6 at a=9.5,x=0.35 vs an independent high-precision series). The port was right and the ORACLE was wrong. Driver now composes Gamma(a)*P(a,x).

title: PETIR: port gsl_sf_expint_E1 and gsl_sf_gamma_inc (unblocks ACER LF=12)

description:
Raised 2026-08-12 from op-62vf.

InterfacialForce::VirtualMass in crates/outram-foam-multiphase/src/two_fluid.rs is a documented scaffold whose momentum_coefficient returns MultiphaseError::NotImplemented. Beads op-dt3.12/.13 require the 1-D closures to TRACE BACK to this crate rather than be invented, and every other closure the new six-equation solver uses does: drag through DragModel::k_d, heat transfer through InterfacialHeatTransfer::volumetric_coefficient_si.

Virtual mass is the one exception, and it is the exception that matters most, because it IS the regularisation the whole six-equation model rests on (see crates/tampines/docs/six-equation-regularisation.md). tampines::multiphase_1d::two_fluid::virtual_mass_coefficient therefore writes the formula down locally:

    K_vm = max(alpha_d, alpha_res) * C_vm * rho_c

transcribed from OpenFOAM dispersedVirtualMassModel.C:51-67 and constantVirtualMassCoefficient.C:71-79 via the source study, with the deviation stated in that function's doc comment rather than hidden.

TO CLOSE: port the dispersedVirtualMassModel chain into outram-foam-multiphase -- the constantCoefficient arm at minimum, and the Lamb aspect-ratio arm (Lamb.C:69-77) if the aspect ratio is available -- so InterfacialForce::VirtualMass returns a real coefficient. Then replace the body of tampines::multiphase_1d::two_fluid::virtual_mass_coefficient with a call into it. Nothing else in the 1-D solver changes; the function exists precisely so that is a one-place edit.

Pinned meanwhile by two_fluid_tests::virtual_mass_coefficient_matches_the_transcribed_upstream_form, which checks the floored and role-swapped forms against hand arithmetic, so a ported version can be diffed against a known-good transcription rather than against nothing.
title: outram-foam-multiphase: port the virtual-mass closure so tampines can consume it instead of transcribing it

description:
RAFFLES (Risk Analysis Framework For Learning & Ensemble Simulation) — crates/raffles. Independent pure-Rust port of the uncertainty-quantification and risk-analysis core of RAVEN (https://github.com/idaholab/raven, Apache-2.0, Idaho National Laboratory).

OWNER: Adolphus Lye (colleague of the maintainer; chose the backronym). Direction, scope and priorities for this crate are theirs to set. Use they/them.

LICENSING: upstream Apache-2.0 -> RAFFLES GPL-3.0-only is ONE-WAY. Code may flow RAVEN -> RAFFLES, never RAFFLES -> RAVEN. Never open a PR against idaholab/raven from this workspace. Verbatim upstream LICENSE.txt/NOTICE.txt preserved as crates/raffles/LICENSE-APACHE-RAVEN and NOTICE-RAVEN; provenance in crates/raffles/NOTICE. Reference commit 01216937967c38ee287859270c035c8eca906dc6 (devel, 2026-07-14), accessed 2026-08-06. NOTE: RAVEN vendors third-party BSD code (AMSC/Univ. of Utah, NGL) near the sensitivity area — those files need BSD headers, not Apache.

SCAFFOLD LANDED 2026-08-06 (uncommitted at time of writing): Cargo.toml (thiserror only, Android-clean), lib.rs + four stub modules, README (Bookkeeping status both axes at X / INCOMPLETE), crate CLAUDE.md, NOTICE + upstream licence files, upstream_source/README.md, added to root Cargo.toml members. Verified: cargo check --workspace --lib; cargo check -p raffles --all-targets --target aarch64-linux-android; pandoc clean on both markdown files.

DESIGN: RAVEN is deeply inheritance-based; sampler/distribution hierarchies MUST become enums, not trait objects (workspace rule). No Box<T>, no lifetime params. Android-clean: no ndarray-linalg/BLAS/C/Fortran; prefer pure-Rust faer if linear algebra is needed.

Scoping doc: docs/raven-port-scoping.md (written separately).
